An outer represents groups of folds on which a specific fold was left out of training and only used for testing. For instance the “outer1” model was trained using all folds except fold1 and then tested on fold1.

LS-GKM SVM Params

LS-GKM SVM stands for large-scale, gapped k-mer support vector machine. This model uses a gapped-kmer tool to extract sequence features than can be used to train the vector machine. The following params were used:

  • alphabet size( \({b}\)): 4
  • 1X negative synthetic data created from positive regulatory sequences
  • \({\ell}\)-mer with truncated function
  • \({\ell}\)-mer size (\({\ell}\)): 11
  • number of informative columns (\({k}\)): 7
  • max umber of mismatches: 4

The GKM tool creates a matrix M by N, where M is the number of all the possible gapped-kmer combinations, given \({\ell}\) and \({k}\), and N the total number of ungapped possibilites. The number of features depends on \({k}\), \({\ell}\), and \({b}\):

\[M = \binom{\ell}{k} b^k\]

Interpretation

The pooled out-of-fold ROC AUC was 0.838, while the mean ROC AUC across the five outer folds was 0.838 ± 0.006.

The pooled average precision was 0.825, compared with a positive prevalence of 0.500. The mean average precision across folds was 0.825 ± 0.007.

ROC AUC ranged from 0.829 in outer1 to 0.843 in outer5. Average precision ranged from 0.814 in outer1 to 0.831 in outer2.

At the fixed decision threshold of 0.00, pooled sensitivity was 0.771 and pooled specificity was 0.745. These values describe performance at this specific threshold and should be interpreted separately from ROC AUC and average precision.

Differences between folds may reflect variation in the chromosome groups assigned to each held-out fold. Fold-level variability should therefore be considered alongside the pooled result rather than relying on the pooled result alone.
